questions.q: What are drone rules usually built around?
questions.explain: Mass, proximity to people, altitude, visibility: categories are defined by the level of risk.

options: Flight altitude no higher than 120 m
questions.explain: Visual Line Of Sight is the baseline requirement of the open category; BVLOS requires separate authorizations.

questions.q: Do the rules apply to an engineer's test flights?
options: No, if you fly on your own land without a camera, as a test
Yes, a test flight is a flight like any other
Only for aircraft heavier than 25 kg
questions.explain: The rules cover any flight, whatever its purpose.

questions.q: What is the only reliable source of the rules?
questions.explain: Rules change every year; only the regulator gives you the current version.

questions.q: What is regulated separately from the flight rules?
options: Battery type and number of motors
questions.explain: Radio frequency law sets the allowed bands and power.

options: The firmware requires it to unlock
questions.explain: The log is proof of discipline and the basis for incident analysis.

questions.q: The EASA Open category is limited to:
questions.explain: Subcategories A1/A2/A3; homebuilt aircraft — A1 (< 250 g) or A3.

questions.q: Typical altitude limit in the open category:
questions.explain: Many regulators limit the open category to ~120 m (400 ft); check your country's rules.
